candidates.title: Map resume details into application fields

demandEvidence.chore: filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

experimentPlan.output: A checked draft mapping of supplied resume facts to a few manually supplied application fields.
inputs: Synthetic resume facts without personal data
Manually supplied sample application field labels
A mapping table of expected field types
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one sample resume and a blank set of application fields.
steps: List facts in the synthetic resume.
Compare each field label with available facts.
Draft one value per clearly matched field.
Have a person review and enter approved values.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic resume and sample fields, every drafted value must match its source fact and every unmatched field must be flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies redacted test inputs, checks each mapping, handles sensitive real applicant data outside the prototype, and submits every form.
unverified: No supplied source supports reading resumes or interacting with application forms.
Company-specific field interpretation and live browser entry are untested.

ease.reason: A beginner can test field mapping with supplied resume and sample form text; no form-filling capability is documented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers might pay to reduce repeated form entry; this post does not establish willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can prepare values for manually supplied fields; company-specific forms and live entry remain untested.

autonomy.reason: The proposed mapping can draft values, but no implementation support is attached and a person must check and submit each form.

evidence.reason: The post states a daily two-hour resume-entry chore for forms tailored to one or two companies.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a draft-only experiment; provisional mean is below six because implementation and buyer evidence are absent.

candidates.title: Prepare daily multi-service order summaries

demandEvidence.chore: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.

experimentPlan.output: A daily draft listing counts and concise summaries for completed, canceled and pending sample orders.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a daily batch using supplied sample order rows.
steps: Check that each row has a status.
Group rows by status and optional service category.
Count rows in each group with the documented Summarize capability.
Draft a short report with the count and supplied date.
Compare totals with input rows and flag unknown statuses.
Have an operator review before sharing.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic dataset, status counts and their total must match a manual count, and unknown statuses must appear in a flagged list.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and validates records, resolves ambiguous statuses, confirms the report, and decides where to share it; use fictional data only.
unverified: No source documents connection to real multi-service order systems.
The reference supports aggregation, not natural-language report accuracy or scheduled delivery.

ease.reason: A beginner can test grouped counts on synthetic order rows; the n8n Summarize reference supports count, sum and grouping by fields, with no live data connection documented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: multi-service operators may pay for daily reporting help; this exploratory post establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample-data report is scopeable; the n8n Summarize reference supports grouped counts, but source integrations and report delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed batch can group and summarize supplied rows using the n8n Summarize reference; scheduling and automated data access are not established.

evidence.reason: The post names daily summaries of completed, canceled and pending orders, but provides no fields, examples or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete daily-summary idea scored with the supplied n8n Summarize reference; its provisional mean is below six.

candidates.title: Map CRM arrays into invoice rows

demandEvidence.chore: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.

experimentPlan.output: A draft invoice-row payload from synthetic Airtable-like arrays for operator inspection.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies sample arrays and the expected row shape for a mapping review.
steps: Read the supplied array names and lengths.
Use the documented indexed mapping concept to identify elements.
Draft row objects for the supplied sample only.
Flag length mismatches or missing labels.
Compare every draft value with its input.
Have a person approve any real endpoint request separately.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed two-item synthetic example, each drafted row must preserve its source amount and tax value, and an independent manual comparison must find no omitted or extra values.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person defines the destination schema, validates amounts and tax treatment, approves any real request, and confirms invoice persistence; the prototype must not issue real invoices.
unverified: The reference does not document dynamically generating invoice rows from arrays.
HTTP endpoint execution, invoice persistence and tax correctness are not established.

ease.reason: A beginner can reproduce indexed array mapping using the Make array-mapping reference; it documents selecting an array element, not dynamic invoice row construction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: automation consultants may pay for mapping help; this troubleshooting post proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic payload mock can compare source arrays with manually assembled rows; the Make reference covers indexed array access only.

autonomy.reason: A proposed transform can draft a payload from supplied arrays, but the Make reference does not establish dynamic row creation, endpoint execution or invoice persistence; human review is required.

evidence.reason: The retained post context names Airtable CRM arrays, multiple invoice rows and a mapping problem, with a small two-value example.

candidates.reason: Specific mapping chore assessed against the supplied Make mapping reference; the narrow documented capability does not support the full requested dynamic invoice workflow, so the mean remains below six.

rejected.title: Create AI creator-style product videos
rejected.reason: The supplied post text defines AI UGC video creation but does not state a concrete requested chore or unmet need; treating this description as demand would invent one.

rejected.title: Enable the Execute Command node
rejected.reason: The retained spans describe a one-off n8n node availability/configuration troubleshooting report, not a repeated business chore; proposing a support service from this bug report would invent recurring demand.

rejected.reason: Duplicate: the specific ecommerce customer and order-status communication workflow match prior post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6. The recent task/context spans describe incomplete or changing order data and customer-facing status updates.

steps.message: Assessed all eight assigned discussion identities. Three concrete chores received scoped plans and five provisional scores; their means remain below 6. Excluded three vague descriptions and a one-off troubleshooting report for lack of a concrete repeated chore, and excluded one ecommerce order-status workflow as duplicate of prior post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6. No post proposed.
